translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Map twenty key RA1 terms about ship parts, vessel types, equipment and port professions through Word Wall Active and a collaborative semantic map. To develop the activity, the instructor will explain the five canon functional categories that organise the vocabulary of a banana reefer vessel and will project the silhouette of the vessel sectioned by colours. Then learners will form teams of four around kraft paper sheets size A1, each team with an envelope of twenty term cards, twenty definition cards and visual icons of Puerto Antioquia. For seventy-five minutes the teams will rotate through three stations: term-image matching, pronunciation with native audio and mirror talking in pairs, and minimal sentence production with the verb to be and demonstratives. The activity ends with a plenary share of twenty-five minutes where each team presents one category drawn at random.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Induce the pattern of five RA1 grammatical structures (verb to be affirmative and negative, demonstratives this/that/these/those, plurals -s/-es, there is/there are with numerical quantification and articles a/an/the) from an authentic corpus of the banana cold chain universe. To develop the activity, the instructor will project a corpus of twelve canon sentences contextualised in bay 14 of the reefer vessel and will invite learners to notice what changes and what stays the same, without explaining rules in advance. Then learners will form teams of four with a canon envelope of twenty sentence cards (ten correct and ten with an introduced error) and a blank sheet to formulate five rules in their own words. For seventy minutes the teams will rotate through two stations: corpus analysis with cards, and sentence building with scrambled word cards. The activity ends with a plenary share of the rules formulated by each team and the delivery of laminated mini-cards with the five consolidated rules.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Read and understand the foundational technical text 'MV CARIBBEAN STAR Arrives at Puerto Antioquia · Meet the Reefer Crew' to identify ship parts, types of merchant vessels, navigational equipment and banana port professions. To develop the activity, the instructor will introduce the DRTA strategy combined with K-W-L and Story Map, will activate prior schemata with questions and will review the Word Wall Active from S2. Then learners will form teams of three with assigned roles (Reader, Mapper and Word-Wizard), each team with a printed copy of the reading, the bilingual K-W-L template and the Story Map. During the reading, the team will do two DRTA passes with strategic pauses to predict, identify vessel features, container types and bay quantities, and to record fifteen key terms. The activity ends with the individual Cuestionario No 1 of five items in thirty minutes followed by a HOTS closure of fifteen minutes with divergent questions.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Reinforce auditory recognition of port vocabulary and bay counting through guided listening of a ninety-second Reefer Yard Walk audio with authentic Colombian banana accent. To develop the activity, the instructor will present the panorama of the audio and the logic of active listening in three passes: general comprehension, focus on lexical vocabulary, and focus on auditory chunking of there is/are phrases with quantifiers. Then learners will form teams of three and will receive a printed bilingual template with four columns: bays mentioned, containers identified, professionals assigned and cold chain status. Next, learners will do the three passes: notes on the general panorama, Sentence Bingo of plurals and demonstratives, and Delayed Repetition choral of bay counts. The activity ends with a brief plenary share of fifteen minutes comparing the templates team by team.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Produce a one-page technical Inspection Report on the walk-around of bay 14 of the reefer vessel applying port vocabulary and A1.2-A1.3 grammar structures. To develop the activity, the instructor will explain the Inspection Report genre as a professional banana document and will model on the board the four key linguistic resources: verb to be affirmative and negative, plurals with numerical quantification, imperative in safety commands and the preposition IN for location. Then learners will form teams of three with TBLT roles (Drafter, Editor and Verifier) and each team will receive the printed bilingual Inspection Report template. During the drafting, the teams will collaboratively complete the template in two passes, integrating bay status description, plurals with counting, safety commands in the imperative and the preposition IN. The activity ends with the individual delivery of the report (each learner signs their copy) evaluated with Lista de Verificación No 2.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Identify correct messages and distractors in an authentic VHF audio of one hundred and five seconds applying the IMO SMCP protocol. To develop the activity, the instructor will present the operational panorama of the audio and will explain the technical components to recognise: eight SMCP message markers, five critical standard responses, clarification phrases, NATO Phonetic Alphabet applied to the call sign and the Over/Out protocol. Then learners will form teams of three with differentiated information assignment: one learner captures the message markers, another captures the standard responses and the third captures the NATO Phonetic spelling and clarification requests. Next, the audio will be played in three controlled passes with visual support gradually removed and cross-verification at the end. The activity ends with the delivery of the individual template evaluated with Lista de Chequeo No 3 and a plenary debrief about the critical points of the SMCP.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Anticipate and reconstruct the operational commands and the canon modal verbs of the tripartite berthing through predictive listening and collaborative reconstruction of an audio of one hundred and ten seconds of coordination during the approach manoeuvre to berth three. To develop the activity, the instructor will present the operational panorama of the audio with four simultaneous actors modelling the four RA3 knowledge points (commands to addressees, safety imperatives, present simple, modals) plus three extensions (type one conditional, passive voice, present perfect). Then learners will form teams of three with a Predictive Listening template of four rows and four columns. Next, the audio will be played once complete and then a second time with strategic pauses at four predictive markers. The activity ends with collaborative reconstruction in light Dictogloss style by blocks in plenary and a debrief of fifteen minutes.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Execute the five canon IMARPOR master functions through timed rotation in a Role Carousel of five physical stations arranged in the classroom, applying tag questions in active production, present progressive with prepositional phrases, quantifiers and six canon discourse connectors (and, but, or, because, so, although). To develop the activity, the instructor will present the panorama of the five canon master functions and will configure the classroom with five separate physical stations arranged in a circle, each station labelled with its master function and contextualised visual prompts. Then learners will rotate individually through the five stations with a strict timed duration of twelve minutes per station. At each station each learner will orally produce the corresponding master function integrating mandatorily the associated grammar structure and at least two connectors. The activity ends with a plenary share of thirty minutes with structured debrief, evaluated with Escala de Estimación No 5 individual.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Produce the four canon RA4 structures (affirmative and negative tag questions, present progressive with prepositional phrases, definite and indefinite quantifiers, geographical prepositional phrases) plus discourse connectors through data-based discovery, sentence building and descriptive chain story. To develop the activity, the instructor will project a corpus of eight canon exchanges from the bay 14 handover and will invite learners to notice the inverted polarity pattern in tag questions plus the rising/falling intonation. Then learners will form teams of four around an A3 satellite map of Puerto Antioquia with movable markers, each team with a triple-layer envelope: twelve sentence cards, eighteen scrambled word cards and six dice of quantifiers. For forty minutes they will rotate through three stations: data-based discovery tag questions, sentence building present progressive, and chain story with quantifiers and connectors. The activity ends with a plenary share of chain stories and the delivery of laminated cards with the four canon structures.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Integrate the canon grammar structures of the four apropiación blocks plus grammar extensions in a cross-RAP rehearsal of the Pre-Departure Banana Reefer Compliance Check scenario with non-graded formative feedback. To develop the activity, the instructor will explain that the structures of the four blocks must operate simultaneously without compartmentalisation and that this is an affective zone of safe rehearsal prior to the capstone. Then learners will form crews of six with operational roles rotating every forty minutes, each crew with a triple-layer dossier: a table of the eighteen structures, a formative feedback guide of seven checks and a four-phase scenario. For four hours and twenty minutes the crews will rotate through three integrated cross-RAP rehearsal stations: initial multi-actor briefing, reefer inspection and safety walkaround, and tripartite pre-departure handover. The activity ends with a plenary share and consolidated feedback of three phases per crew.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Appropriate the operational scenario of the integrative capstone where the crew will execute the real banana reefer dispatch journey in ninety timed minutes before an external evaluation panel of three people. To develop the activity, the instructor will project the map of Puerto Antioquia with marked bays, the contextual photo of the vessel berthed at berth 3 and the organisation chart of the evaluation panel. Then learners will form the operational crews of six already assigned in S10 and each team will receive three printed physical documents: the two-page Mission Brief, the capstone PBL Rubric of six criteria and the confirmed role assignment sheet. Next, a structured Q&A session will be held where each crew will present three critical questions to the teaching panel. The activity ends with the symbolic signature of the role assignment by each learner and the delivery of a personalised schedule.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Collaboratively design the three intermediate deliverables of the crew that will be executed before the panel: the visitor checklist banana cold chain for the reefer yard walk, the VHF script SMCP arrival/departure exchange, and the handover meeting pitch outline with anticipated Q&A. To develop the activity, the instructor will recall the canon resources available since apropiación (Word Wall Active of eighty terms, SMCP pocket cards, Pre-Shipment templates and anonymised ICA certificate) and will clarify that each crew designs its own artefacts without receiving pre-resolved templates. Then within each crew of six the work will be distributed according to the assigned roles: two learners draft the visitor checklist, two design the VHF script and two build the handover pitch outline. Next, the learners will hold focused technical consultations with the mentors available in the classroom. The activity ends with internal consolidation in a single triple printed deliverable and a brief sixty-second share per crew.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Execute the complete rehearsal of the ninety-minute operational journey in each of the six crews with non-graded formative feedback from the teaching team to correct SMCP errors in the zero-tolerance zone and refine the fluency of the handover meeting before the evaluated Performance. To develop the activity, the instructor will explain the two differentiated feedback modes: immediate interruptive correction in the SMCP accuracy zone, and deferred fluency-friendly debrief correction for everything else. Then learners will form the six crews in scheduled order and each one will execute its complete ninety minutes in three internal phases in front of the other crews as silent audience: reefer yard walk of thirty minutes, VHF bridge call of twenty minutes, and tripartite handover meeting of forty minutes. The activity ends with a rapid five-minute VHF drill per crew with an unexpected situation and the delivery of individualised written formative feedback in a sealed envelope.

translations.descripcion_aprendiz_en: Close the complete twelve-session programme by articulating a structured debrief per crew with panel feedback, certification recognition, formal delivery of diplomas and a celebratory ritual that preserves the cold chain integrity as symbolic pedagogical compliance. To develop the activity, the instructor will open the session by projecting a visual timeline of the programme and will facilitate the initial reflection by asking how the person who entered in S1 feels and how the person who leaves in S12 feels. Then learners will form the crews in reverse order to the Performance for the structured panel debrief of fifteen minutes per crew, receiving technical feedback, feedback on cold chain integrity and feedback on reefer yard safety. Next, each learner will share an individual round of ninety seconds about a moment when they felt that operational English was possible. The activity ends with the formal delivery of diplomas, a pocket card of professional continuity and a closing group photo.
